summary: The exact candidate adds a working opt-in persistent worklist to the actual MoE GEMM1 path while preserving the default API, 2-D launch behavior, and numerical result. The missing opt-in fails on the recorded base and passes candidate plus independent gfx950 GPU tests.

tests.what_was_measured: Recorded-base failing-before: the real GEMM1 API rejects persistent=True with an unexpected-keyword TypeError.
Recorded-base default-path health: 12/12 numerical cases passed on gfx950.
Exact-candidate regression: 8/8 persistent masked-tail cases passed across all four supported input formats.
Broad candidate GEMM1 suite: 205 passed and 96 skipped.

Independent Torch-reference and default-mode comparisons for underfilled and repeated worklists, masked tails, tile_n 64/128/256, multipliers 1/2/3, f16/bf16, and fp8/int8/int8smooth/int4; also invalid multiplier rejection and NaN completion guards.
Exact candidate harness: eight numerical pairs and warmed GPU-event timing with 20 warmups and seven 100-launch batches.
Candidate Python syntax and patch whitespace.

gpu_evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, 256 compute units; real GEMM1 kernels compiled and executed with Torch-reference comparisons.
remaining_limitations: Only gfx950 execution was available; gfx94-family execution remains unverified.
Synthetic timing was variable and usually slower for persistent mode; no performance speedup is established.
No native C++ source changed, so the pinned native rebuild was not applicable.
The upstream issue was fetched through the public API after the configured token was rejected by ROCm organization policy; the fetched text matched the supplied issue snapshot.
